resolvedBlockers.summary: POST /devices/entities/devices/v2 returns HTTP 400 for a 250-AID batch on the live tenant, while the single-AID access probe returns 200. Run publishes nothing (correct by design) but cannot complete.
candidateCauses: one or more submitted IDs rejected by the vendor
resolvedBlockers.favours: second cause - the 400 body carries a populated resources array with a valid device entity
resolvedBlockers.neededToDecide: Run one findings collection with aidBatchSize=2-3 (Collectors:FalconCollector:Credentials in appsettings.local.json). A 250-AID response is ~1MB so errors[] cannot fit a log budget; shrinking the request is the only way to see it. Success => per-request ID cap (chunk the lookup; assets sends up to 1000 and is more exposed). Failure with visible errors[] => rejected identifiers (stop sending non-AID ids derived by AidExtractor).
resolvedBlockers.notFixedBecause: the two candidate remedies diverge, and consuming a partial-success 400 risks publishing hosts that DO have a policy as having none
resolvedBlockers.sharedDefectFound: StreamedResponseBodyReader.ReadFirstCharsAsync did a single ReadAsync, so maxErrorSnippetChars was never reached on chunked responses - every collector's vendor error snippet was cut to ~one buffer. Fixed with a read loop; locked by StreamedResponseBodyReaderTests (verified failing against the old implementation).
resolvedBlockers.rootCause: AidExtractor falls back to the 32-hex suffix of Discover's combined `id` when no `aid` field exists. For unmanaged/unsupported Discover entities that suffix is a well-formed 32-hex value that is NOT an agent id; CrowdStrike rejects it as 'invalid device id'. In the failing window 333 of 374 sent identifiers (89%) were such non-AIDs.
resolvedBlockers.capHypothesisDead: FalconPy endpoint table (from CrowdStrike OpenAPI): PostDeviceDetailsV2 supports up to 5000 ids. 250 is far below it. The POC's batch_size=5000 default was never exercised (samples 5 hosts per policy) and sourced real AIDs from policy members, never Discover.
resolvedBlockers.liveProof: A) 41 managed aid values -> HTTP 200, 41 resources, 0 errors. B) 2 id-suffix heuristic values -> HTTP 400 'invalid device id'. C) 1 managed + 1 heuristic -> HTTP 400 with 1 resource + 1 error, reproducing the production shape.
resolvedBlockers.agreedFix: Only identifiers sourced from the real aid/device_id field may reach the device endpoint; hosts whose aid exists only via the id-suffix heuristic get the complete/prevention:null envelope with no vendor call. Do not chunk (cap is 5000) and do not add 400-tolerance.
resolvedBlockers.resolution: Only explicitly-stated AIDs (aid/device_id) reach the device endpoint via new AidExtractor.ExtractSensorAid; the combined-id derivation is retained only as the best-effort AID for Spotlight scoping. DiscoverHost carries both. Access probe now requests a managed entity (+entity_type:'managed') and no longer duplicates across validation and init.
resolvedBlockers.liveVerification: CollectFindings: Success=True, 374 hosts, 78933 findings; 396 records all collection_status=complete; 63 resolved records (41 managed hosts + 22 extra chunks), 333 prevention:null. CollectAssets: Success=True, 375 records all complete, 41 resolved = every managed host, 0 duplicated device_policies properties.
